issues.label: AOM statutory compliance
issues.why: Court must decide whether the affidavit of merit satisfied MCL 600.2912d at filing.

issues.label: Signer qualified under 2169
issues.why: Court must determine whether Dr. Bal met MCL 600.2169’s matching-specialty and time-devoted requirements.

issues.label: Relevant one-year period
issues.why: Court must identify the correct one-year window for the 'majority of professional time' inquiry under MCL 600.2169.

issues.label: Clinical practice vs teaching
issues.why: Court must decide whether Dr. Bal devoted a majority of time to clinical practice or teaching (or neither) in the relevant year.

issues.label: Effect of retirement
issues.why: Court must assess whether alleged retirement in 2017 defeats statutory qualification for a 2019 event.

issues.label: AOM statements truthfulness
issues.why: Court must determine whether contrary evidence shows Dr. Bal’s AOM assertions about practice/teaching were false.

issues.label: Burden on AOM challenge
issues.why: Court must allocate burdens of production/persuasion when defendants challenge AOM validity on summary disposition.

issues.label: Permissible evidence on motion
issues.why: Court must decide whether transcripts/LinkedIn from other matters are admissible/usable under MCR 2.116 standards.

issues.label: Credibility vs qualification
issues.why: Court must distinguish an improper credibility attack from a proper statutory-qualification challenge.

issues.label: Procedural posture: discovery closed
issues.why: Court must consider the 'put up or shut up' principle after close of discovery when evaluating evidentiary showings.

issues.label: Sanction for nonproduction
issues.why: Court must consider consequences of plaintiff’s failure to produce Dr. Bal for deposition as ordered.

issues.label: Enforcement of deposition order
issues.why: Court must decide whether contempt/sanctions, issue preclusion, or dismissal are warranted for violating the deposition order.

issues.label: Need to depose AOM affiant
issues.why: Court must address whether defendants are entitled to depose Dr. Bal despite plaintiff withdrawing him as a trial expert.

issues.label: Withdrawal of expert effect
issues.why: Court must decide whether removing Dr. Bal from witness list affects the already-filed AOM’s validity.

issues.label: Relation between AOM and experts
issues.why: Court must consider whether plaintiff may rely on a different trial expert than the AOM signer without curing AOM defects.

issues.label: Amend witness list standard
issues.why: Court must apply MCR 2.401(I)(2) to determine if amendment to substitute Dr. Hall is allowed.

issues.label: Good cause for amendment
issues.why: Court must decide whether plaintiff showed good cause/diligence for late substitution of an expert.

issues.label: Scheduling order interpretation
issues.why: Court must determine whether the stipulated scheduling extension modified expert/witness disclosure deadlines.

issues.label: Untimely amended witness list
issues.why: Court must address consequences of filing an amended witness list without leave and after deadlines.

issues.label: Dean v Tucker factors
issues.why: Court must weigh Dean factors (willfulness, history, prejudice, notice, lesser sanctions) for exclusion/effective dismissal.

issues.label: Prejudice to defendants
issues.why: Court must assess specific prejudice from late expert substitution (case strategy, facilitation, dispositive motions, trial prep).

issues.label: Ability to cure prejudice
issues.why: Court must consider whether extending deadlines/reopening discovery could cure prejudice and on what terms.

issues.label: Impact on trial date
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether allowing substitution would disrupt the February 2023 trial schedule.

issues.label: Alternative sanctions
issues.why: Court must consider lesser remedies than exclusion/dismissal (costs, adjournment, limited deposition, reopened discovery).

issues.label: Facilitation fairness
issues.why: Court must consider whether late substitution undermines the parties’ ability to conduct meaningful facilitation/ADR.

issues.label: Voluntary dismissal prerequisites
issues.why: Court must apply MCR 2.504(A) to determine whether dismissal without prejudice is procedurally available.

issues.label: Court-ordered dismissal authority
issues.why: Court must decide whether to grant voluntary dismissal by order and under what conditions (costs, fees, prejudice).

issues.label: Discretion to deny dismissal
issues.why: Court must decide whether defendants would suffer legal prejudice warranting denial of voluntary dismissal.

issues.label: Avoiding adverse ruling
issues.why: Court must consider whether plaintiff seeks dismissal to evade pending dispositive motions and whether that constitutes prejudice.

issues.label: Statute of limitations tolling
issues.why: Court must consider the practical effect of dismissal on refiling (limitations, savings statute, notice of intent tolling).

issues.label: AOM defect curable by refiling
issues.why: Court must address whether dismissal would allow plaintiff to cure an invalid AOM and whether that is permissible or unfairly prejudicial.

issues.label: Mandatory dismissal for invalid AOM
issues.why: Court must determine whether an invalid AOM requires dismissal as a matter of law and whether it must be with prejudice.

issues.label: With or without prejudice
issues.why: Court must decide the proper form of dismissal if AOM is invalid (including effect of limitations and savings provisions).

issues.label: Summary disposition rule invoked
issues.why: Court must identify the proper MCR 2.116 ground (C)(10) and apply its standards to the AOM-qualification dispute.

issues.label: Genuine issue of material fact
issues.why: Court must decide whether plaintiff produced evidence creating a factual dispute on Dr. Bal’s qualification.

issues.label: Plaintiff reasonable belief argument
issues.why: Court must decide whether 'reasonable belief' can substitute for actual statutory compliance with AOM requirements.

issues.label: Consideration of counsel diligence
issues.why: Court must assess plaintiff’s diligence in vetting expert qualifications and pursuing discovery as it bears on discretion and sanctions.

issues.label: Effect on vicarious claims
issues.why: Court must determine whether dismissal/summary disposition on malpractice claim disposes of vicarious liability claims against Tri County/Beaumont.

issues.label: Separate defendant positions
issues.why: Court must address whether Beaumont and Tri County defendants are similarly situated and entitled to identical relief.

issues.label: Agency/employee relationship relevance
issues.why: Court must consider whether employment/agency facts affect vicarious liability and any independent claims against hospital/practice entity.

issues.label: Order of motion sequencing
issues.why: Court must decide whether to resolve amendment/dismissal requests before or after ruling on summary disposition and why.

issues.label: Reopening discovery authority
issues.why: Court must consider whether it has authority to reopen discovery to cure AOM/qualification disputes and under what standards.

issues.label: Reconsideration standards
issues.why: Court must apply standards for reconsideration (palpable error/new evidence) to any renewed requests.

issues.label: Record adequacy
issues.why: Court must ensure the factual record is adequate to decide qualification and prejudice issues without evidentiary hearing if one is required.

issues.label: Need for evidentiary hearing
issues.why: Court must decide whether resolving conflicting evidence on Dr. Bal’s practice/teaching requires an evidentiary hearing.

issues.label: Authentication of online evidence
issues.why: Court must consider authentication/reliability of LinkedIn and similar materials used to challenge qualifications.

issues.label: Use of prior sworn testimony
issues.why: Court must decide how to treat deposition/trial testimony from other cases (admissions, hearsay exceptions, impeachment) at summary disposition.

issues.label: Expert disclosure vs AOM timing
issues.why: Court must consider that AOM is required at filing and cannot be retroactively satisfied by later expert substitution.

issues.label: Equitable considerations
issues.why: Court must consider fairness and case-management equities when ruling on discretionary relief (amendment, dismissal, sanctions).
